issues.description: The template's class header for Bitmap24 does not declare a default (no-argument) constructor, while Bitmap24.cpp in the template defines one and main.cpp instantiates Bitmap24 with the default constructor (Bitmap24 bitmap;). The solution repository's Bitmap24.hpp does declare the default constructor. This mismatch (header vs. implementation and header vs. usage in main) will cause compilation failures or confusion for students: main expects a publicly-declared default constructor but the template class declaration omits it.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a declaration for the default constructor to the template header so the class declaration matches its implementation and usage. For example, in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp add 'Bitmap24();' (public) above or alongside the existing parameterized constructor declaration. This will align the template with the solution and allow 'Bitmap24 bitmap;' in main.cpp to compile.
